Voynich MS - Quire 17

General

For an explanation of the material found on this page, see here.

Description

Quire 17 contains folios 93 through 96. Folio 95 is a foldout folio. The gathering mark is on f96v. A parchment strip was sewn in in addition (visible between folios 94 and 95).

Schematic folio layout:

Folio 93

Normal folio. The folio nr. is on f93r.

f93r  

>>Link to 2014 scan (Beinecke digital library)

>>Link to 2004 scan (Jason Davies Voyager)

General description

This is a herbal page. For general information about herbal pages see here.
It has the folio nr (93) in the upper right corner.

Illustration(s)

Drawing of a single plant. It has simple roots with some red paint, a single vertical stem with cresent leaves arranged symmetrically, and a single 'pod' painted light brown with many dots arranged in radii from the centre.

Herbal drawing characterisation (Gheuens/Rapaport):
(none)

Text

This page has 32 text items (loci), as follows:
32 lines of standard text in paragraphs;

The text is arranged in a single paragraph. All lines end at the plant drawing, and many are short. The text fills almost all space not occupied by the drawing.

Currier language: A
RZ language: A (page) / A (folio) / Ae (bifolio)
LFD hand: 1

Browse interlinear transliteration of f93r

Tentative identifications

O'Neill: sunflower (helianthus). ThP: (like coxcomb?).

Other information

This is the famous 'sunflower' mentioned in a publication by O'Neill. This has been used as evidence that the MS should date from after Columbus' second trip to America, when Sunflowers were first seen in Europe. This identification is not generally accepted.

General description

This is a herbal page. For general information about herbal pages see here.

Large plant drawing on the right hand side of the page. Root with large brown bulbs. Single vertical stem. Six leaves arranged symmetrically with large 'fingers'. No flowers, but three sets of 8 red currants.

α: stalk connects to leaf centre

α: berries that have no added circles

General description

This is a herbal page. For general information about herbal pages see here.

Illustration(s)

Plant drawing with roots including large tubers painted in two shades of brown, and with a single small hole in the side of each. There are many simple pointed leaves radiating out in several shades of green. A single stem going up ends in a green bulb and a small flower with blue/green painting.

This plant shows some similarity with plant fragment #22 on f88v.

Herbal drawing characterisation (Gheuens/Rapaport):
β: 'grass'

General description

This is a herbal page. For general information about herbal pages see here.
It has the folio nr (96) in the upper right corner.

Illustration(s)

A very large plant drawing. The roots have many items looking almost like leaves, with rows of dots along the middle. The roots are painted very light brow. A single stem with two thicker parts, one spherical and one elongated. Eight rather large starry leaves, and a very large bulb at the top, curving down. This has been inaccurately and ligtly painted in some indeterminate brown and/or blue shade.

Herbal drawing characterisation (Gheuens/Rapaport):
α: stalk connects to leaf centre
α: feature interrupts the main stem

Text

This page has 13 text items (loci), as follows:
13 lines of standard text in paragraphs;

The text is in a single paragraph at the top of the page. All lines end at the plant drawing and the last three lines are broken up by one of the leaves of the plant.

Currier language: A
RZ language: Ae (page) / Ae (folio) / Ae (bifolio)
LFD hand: 1

Browse interlinear transliteration of f96r

Tentative identifications

ThP: dipsacus calendula (O'Neill).

General description

This is a herbal page. For general information about herbal pages see here.

Illustration(s)

A very tall plant drawing. A light brown bulbous root with many hairs. A single stem going up, splitting at the top and both ends hanging all the way down. Many triangular leaves and respectively five and six groups of small currants at the end of the stems.

This plant shows some similarity with plant fragment #94 on f99r
and with plant fragment #116 on f100r.

Herbal drawing characterisation (Gheuens/Rapaport):
α: berries that have no added circles

Text

This page has 13 text items (loci), as follows:
13 lines of standard text in paragraphs;

The text is in a single paragraph at the top of the page. The top three lines cover the entire width of the page but are interrupted by the top leaves of the plant. All other lines end at the plant drawing.

Currier language: A
RZ language: Ae (page) / Ae (folio) / Ae (bifolio)
LFD hand: 1

Browse interlinear transliteration of f96v

Tentative identifications

ThP: smilas tracheia or chenopodium (bonus atruplex), good king henry, atruplex or hastata.
